title: The same design, with findings the engine must refuse (SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE)

assumptions.text: If Redis is down when the API publishes, the notification is not lost: it is sent later from the table.
assumptions.quote: if it is not, the notification stays in the table and will be picked up later

evidence.observation: Step 4 deletes the cron job, which is the only reader of the table.

assumptions.text: The provider's rate limit applies per consumer.
assumptions.quote: The email provider accepts at most one message per second per consumer

assumptions.text: The stream never loses a message.
assumptions.quote: Redis Streams guarantee that no message is ever lost
assumptions.check: Read the persistence settings of the Redis deployment.

assumptions.text: Consumers keep up with the stream.
assumptions.quote: A pool of 4 consumers reads the stream through a consumer group
the old `notifications.sent_at` column is dropped in the next migration

evidence.observation: The rollout section says nothing about restoring the column.

attacks.quote: the notification stays in the table and will be picked up later
attacks.attack: If Redis is down when the API publishes, the row stays in the table but nothing reads it once the cron job is gone.
attacks.check: Stop Redis in staging, create 20 notifications, restart Redis and count how many are sent.

attacks.quote: accepts at most one message per second per consumer
attacks.attack: If the provider's limit applies per account, the 4 consumers share it and throttled sends are dropped.
attacks.check: Ask the provider whether the limit is per API key or per connection.

attacks.quote: The stream loses messages when Redis restarts without persistence
attacks.attack: A Redis restart without persistence empties the stream and every pending notification disappears.
attacks.check: Restart Redis in staging with persistence off and count the pending messages.

attacks.quote: accepts at most one message per second per consumer
attacks.attack: If the limit of the provider applies per account, the 4 consumers share it, and throttled sends are dropped.
attacks.check: Ask the provider whether the limit is per API key or per connection.

attacks.quote: publishes its id to a Redis Stream called `notify`
attacks.attack: Nothing limits how many notifications one client can trigger, so one client can flood the stream.

attacks.quote: A pool of 4 consumers reads the stream through a consumer group
attacks.attack: Four consumers cannot drain a campaign of 50,000 messages in useful time.
attacks.check: Compute N / (consumers x rate) for the largest campaign of last quarter.

attacks.quote: the old `notifications.sent_at` column is dropped in the next migration
attacks.attack: Once the column is dropped, reverting the release cannot restore the sent_at data.
attacks.check: Apply the migration in staging and try to revert.
